title: Choose MIMIC's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Movement Score. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Movement Score
options.lineage: Labanotation: dance notation written so another body can perform it
options.thesis: The clip is notated like a dance score, and the robot is the second dancer reading it.
materials: level shading (black low, dot middle, hatch high)
options.viewport: Clip with tracked overlay at left; a vertical staff in the middle with lanes for hand, each object and gripper, steps as blocks whose length is their duration; the arm's 3-D replay at right; Upload and Run on arm in the top bar.
options.risk: Time running up the staff is the form's native grammar but new to most reviewers; it needs clear second ticks to read in one glance.

raised.raise: Fixed cells: a step keeps its cell when its state changes; an issue restyles the row, never reflows the score.
Every tracked object carries one name plate and colour ribbon, used identically on the video, the staff and the 3-D table.
Every claim beside its proof: each step shows its measured millimetres and seconds.
One data size; rank comes from weight, case and reversal, not bigger type.
Running times right-aligned; the program's duration is accounted against the clip's.

regions.label: top bar: MIMIC · upload · run on arm

options.label: Slicer Preview
options.lineage: 3-D printer slicers (Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer) previewing a toolpath
options.thesis: The program previewed like a print: toolpath in 3-D, listing synced to a time slider.
options.viewport: Big 3-D plate with the coloured toolpath; clip as a docked thumbnail; vertical time slider at the right edge; program listing below.
options.risk: The most familiar choice for makers, and where most robotics tools land; the clip becomes secondary.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Each object is a coloured line; picks and places are its stations, carries the runs between.
options.viewport: A midnight diagram strip under the clip, one line per object with stations at each step; 3-D replay beside it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads instantly per object; loses on time, which the diagram deliberately flattens.
options.risk: Durations and simultaneity disappear, and reviewers judge timing.

regions.label: line diagram: one line per object

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Steps as departure rows that flip when they change.
options.viewport: A board of step rows over the clip.
options.risk: Novelty clacks over a review task.
options.case: Demonstrators don't read their work as departures; time and space get lost in rows.
options.kept: Fixed cells: state restyles a row without reflowing the grid.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Tracked objects as a ranked cast of characters.
options.case: Wrong register for a tool; loses both axes.
options.kept: One name plate and colour ribbon per object, everywhere.

options.label: Monochrome Product Marketing
options.thesis: Claim, then the screenshot that proves it.
options.risk: A persuasion form for an operate task.
options.case: Persuade grammar; the reviewer needs the work, not the pitch.
options.kept: Every claim sits beside its measured proof.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: A raked rack of step slides.
options.risk: The rake fights video and 3-D panes.
options.case: Raked containers obscure the three media panes.
options.kept: One data size; hierarchy from weight and case.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: The program as a hand-timed tracklist.
options.viewport: Side A: the person; side B: the robot.
options.case: Hand-lettered ink reads tentative where the check must read certain.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark robotics dashboard: video, JSON and 3-D in equal panels.
canonCard.viewport: Three equal dark panels and a sidebar of steps.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every robotics demo by design.
